q_local_north_forestry.4: Adopt the Working Forest model: zones, no net loss and a 45 million cubic metre objective, $50 million to make rarest old-growth deferrals permanent, and mill retrofits.
q_local_north_forestry.5: Implement the Working Forest Landscape Model: three zones with a 'no net loss' rule and a 45 million cubic metre objective, fewer case-by-case permits, $50 million to convert rarest old-growth deferrals to permanent protection, mill retrofit support for value-added second growth.

q_local_north_forestry.1: Write logging zones into law, sell more public timber, and speed up forestry permits.
q_local_north_forestry.2: Write timber zones into law, sell more public timber, add a fibre task force, and give forestry one-stop permits.
q_local_north_forestry.3: Set Working Forest zones in law with a 45 million cubic metre goal, raise public timber sales, and decide forestry permits in 90 days.
q_local_north_forestry.4: Set Working Forest zones in law, aim for 45 million cubic metres, raise BC Timber Sales to 9 million cubic metres, decide permits in 90 days, and fund workers and mass timber.
q_local_north_forestry.5: Legislate Working Forest zones; work toward 45 million cubic metres, 40 million by 2030; BC Timber Sales to 9 million cubic metres by 2029; a Forestry Fibre Task Force; One-Stop with 90-day decisions; $100 million for workers and mass timber.

q_local_north_forestry.1: Allow more cutting, charge companies less for the wood, and shorten permits and consultations.
q_local_north_forestry.2: Raise the allowed yearly cut further, lower the fees companies pay for public timber, and shorten permit and consultation times.
q_local_north_forestry.3: Raise the allowable annual cut beyond current targets, cut stumpage fees to make mills more competitive, and shorten permit approvals and consultations.
q_local_north_forestry.4: Raise the allowable cut above the current objective, cut stumpage fees for lumber companies, and speed up permits and consultations, with no zoning or old-growth plan.
q_local_north_forestry.5: Increase the allowable annual cut 'to ensure our forest sector has the available wood fibre to grow and thrive', reduce stumpage fees for lumber companies, speed up permit approval times and consultations, with no volume target or old-growth measure.

q_local_north_resources.1: No new gas plants or pipelines; mines only under strict rules that respect First Nations.
q_local_north_resources.2: Stop approving new gas plants, pipelines and fracking expansion, and allow mines only within ecological limits and strict pollution rules.
q_local_north_resources.3: End approvals for new gas export plants, pipelines and fracking expansion, raise royalties, and allow mines only within ecological limits, to strict standards and respecting First Nations' rights.
q_local_north_resources.4: Approve no new fracking, LNG terminals or pipelines, manage a production decline, take 50% of net profits in royalties, and allow mining only within ecological limits.
q_local_north_resources.5: End approvals for new fracking expansion, LNG terminals and pipelines; managed decline of existing production; end subsidies and collect 50% of net profits in royalties; mining only within ecological limits and to world-leading standards, with public support for mineral processing only with First Nations participation, a long-term economic case and pollution standards.

q_local_north_resources.1: Approve projects that can reach zero emissions, speed up permits, build the power line.
q_local_north_resources.2: Approve gas plants that can run net-zero, run permits and reviews at the same time, and fast-track the power line.
q_local_north_resources.3: Require new gas plants to be net-zero ready by 2030, run assessments and permits together, double mineral exports, and fast-track the North Coast line.
q_local_north_resources.4: Keep the net-zero-ready rule and industrial carbon pricing, run reviews and permits together, double critical mineral exports, and fast-track the North Coast line.
q_local_north_resources.5: Keep the 2030 net-zero-ready requirement and industrial carbon pricing, run assessments and permits concurrently, double critical mineral exports, fast-track the North Coast Transmission Line with Canadian steel, and start a $50 million Clean Futures Fund from gas revenue.

q_local_north_resources.1: One-year legal deadline for decisions, with First Nations partners and a zero-emissions plan required.
q_local_north_resources.2: One-year deadline for decisions, gas plants only with First Nations partners and a net-zero plan, ten mine decisions by 2030.
q_local_north_resources.3: Legislate a 12-month decision deadline, back gas plants with First Nations partners and net-zero plans, keep industrial carbon pricing, and decide on ten mines.
q_local_north_resources.4: Decide in 12 months, back LNG only with First Nations partners and a net-zero-ready plan, keep industrial carbon pricing, rule on ten mines by 2030, and fund port access.
q_local_north_resources.5: One coordinated review with a 12-month provincial decision deadline; LNG backed only with First Nations partners and a credible net-zero-ready plan; industrial carbon pricing kept; permitting decisions on ten mines by 2030; $750 million in provincial road and rail links to match a $1.5 billion federal port request.

q_local_north_resources.1: Approve big projects within four months by law, double gas output, drop emissions limits.
q_local_north_resources.2: Pass a law requiring decisions on big projects within 120 days, double gas production by 2032, and drop emissions limits.
q_local_north_resources.3: Legislate 120-day permitting for projects over $250 million, double gas production by 2032, end emissions limits, and fix the North Coast line deadline.
q_local_north_resources.4: Permit big projects in 120 days, double gas output by 2032 and triple it by 2035, drop emissions limits, replace the LNG carbon-tax rules, and set a power line deadline.
q_local_north_resources.5: Enact a 120 Day Permitting Act for projects over $250 million; double LNG production by 2032 and triple by 2035; end emissions limits and replace the LNG carbon-tax framework; expedite Ksi Lisims; fixed deadline for the North Coast line.

q_local_north_resources.1: Approve projects and a coast pipeline without long consultations, and cut fees.
q_local_north_resources.2: Approve major projects without consultations that act as vetoes, approve a pipeline to Prince Rupert or Kitimat, and cut fees.
q_local_north_resources.3: Approve major projects without consultations acting as vetoes, approve a pipeline to Prince Rupert or Kitimat, and reduce fees for mining and forestry.
q_local_north_resources.4: Approve a pipeline to Prince Rupert or Kitimat, end consultations that act as vetoes, cut mining and forestry fees, and work with Alberta and Saskatchewan.
q_local_north_resources.5: Approve major projects without consultations that act as vetoes; approve a pipeline to Prince Rupert or Kitimat 'to get Canadian energy to foreign markets'; reduce fees and speed approvals for mining and forestry; work with Alberta and Saskatchewan on energy.

q_local_north_er.1: Make every closure public, set a target to cut them, and fund fill-in doctors.
q_local_north_er.2: Pass a law reporting every closure, aim to halve closure hours, and fund a pot for fill-in doctors and backup.
q_local_north_er.3: Legislate reporting of every closure, aim to halve closure hours by 2030, fund a rural pot for locums and backup, with permanent retention bonuses.
q_local_north_er.4: Publicly report every closure, halve unplanned closure hours by 2029/30, spend $25 million a year on rural locums and backup, and make the retention bonus permanent.
q_local_north_er.5: Enact an Emergency Room Accountability Act requiring public reporting of every closure, halve unplanned closure hours by 2029/30, fund a $25 million a year rural stabilization fund for locums, travel and virtual backup, and make the rural retention bonus permanent.

q_local_north_er.1: Set up an emergency fund for small-town clinics and emergency rooms about to close.
q_local_north_er.2: Create a $50 million emergency fund for rural practices at risk of closing, loosen staffing rules, and fast-track foreign-trained doctors.
q_local_north_er.3: Create a $50 million emergency fund for rural practices at risk of closing, allow flexible staffing, fast-track credentials, and appoint an expert commission.
q_local_north_er.4: Put $50 million into rural practices at risk of closing, allow flexible staffing, accept other provinces' credentials, hold health spending, and form an expert panel.
q_local_north_er.5: Create a $50 million emergency fund for rural medical practices at risk of closing, flexible staffing to prevent closures, automatic recognition of other provinces' credentials and faster recognition for Canadian doctors trained abroad, an expert commission within 100 days, and no cuts to the 2026 health budget.

q_local_north_er.1: Recruit more doctors with cheaper tuition, loan help and moving money for rural jobs.
q_local_north_er.2: Recruit: tuition discounts, loan forgiveness and moving costs for rural posts, more training seats, and a bridge for foreign-trained doctors.
q_local_north_er.3: Recruit staff through tuition discounts, loan forgiveness and moving costs for rural areas, 1,000 more nursing and care training seats, and a bridging program for international graduates.
q_local_north_er.4: Give rural health workers tuition discounts, loan forgiveness and moving costs, add 1,000 nursing and care seats, help foreign-trained doctors qualify, and open 20 team clinics.
q_local_north_er.5: Recruit through discounted tuition, loan forgiveness and moving expenses for health workers taking rural and emergency posts, 1,000 added training seats for nurses, nurse practitioners, allied health workers and care aides, a bridging-to-practice program for internationally trained doctors, 20 team-based primary care clinics, and eight MRI and ten CT scanners.

q_local_north_er.1: Open a public health centre in every area so fewer people need emergency rooms.
q_local_north_er.2: Open a community health centre in every riding, fund safe nurse-to-patient ratios, phase out private agency nurses, and keep care public.
q_local_north_er.3: Change the model: a community health centre in every riding, funding for safe nurse-to-patient ratios, an end to private agency nurses, a review toward one provincial health authority.
q_local_north_er.4: Fund a community health centre in every riding, fund nurse-to-patient ratios, phase out agency nurses, review a move to one health authority, and keep health dollars public.
q_local_north_er.5: Fund a Community Health Centre in every riding, increase funding for nurses to support safe nurse-to-patient ratios, phase out private agency nurses and for-profit staffing agencies, review the health authority model with a focus on one consolidated provincial authority, and keep every public health dollar in public care.

q_local_north_er.1: Allow private clinics beside public care, and rehire workers who left over vaccine rules.
q_local_north_er.2: Allow private health care alongside public care, and reinstate nurses who lost jobs over vaccine mandates, with back pay.
q_local_north_er.3: Allow private health care alongside public care, reinstate nurses removed under vaccine mandates with back pay, and shift administration spending to the front line.
q_local_north_er.4: Allow private care beside fully funded public care, reinstate nurses removed under vaccine mandates with back pay, and move admin spending to front-line staff.
q_local_north_er.5: Allow private health care alongside fully funded public care, reinstate nurses removed under vaccine mandates with back pay, shift administration and human resources spending to front-line staff, attract medical professionals, and repeal the Health Professions and Occupations Act.

q_cost_of_living.1: Cut income tax by a quarter for everyone, businesses too, and cut sales tax.
q_cost_of_living.2: Cut every income tax rate by a quarter, for people and companies, and lower the sales tax.
q_cost_of_living.3: Cut every income tax rate by 25%, including the rate companies pay, and lower the provincial sales tax.
q_cost_of_living.4: Cut every personal and corporate income tax rate by 25%, and cut the provincial sales tax (PST) by two points.
q_cost_of_living.5: Cut every personal and corporate income tax bracket by 25%, and lower the provincial sales tax (PST) by two percentage points.

q_cost_of_living.1: Raise the amount people can earn before paying income tax. Add no new taxes.
q_cost_of_living.2: Raise the amount you can earn tax-free, so most workers save about $1,000 a year. Add no new taxes.
q_cost_of_living.3: Raise the tax-free amount to $32,000, worth about $1,000 a year for most workers, and add no new taxes.
q_cost_of_living.4: Raise the basic personal amount (income you earn tax-free) to $32,000, about $1,000 per taxpayer, pledge no new taxes, and temporarily remove PST from Canadian alcohol.
q_cost_of_living.5: Raise the basic personal amount from $13,216 to $32,000 (about $1,000 a year per filer, the same for everyone earning over about $40,000), add no new taxes, and temporarily remove PST from Canadian alcohol.

q_cost_of_living.1: Cut the gas tax, limit milk and egg prices, and freeze car insurance rates.
q_cost_of_living.2: Cut the gas tax, limit store markups on milk, eggs and poultry, and freeze car insurance rates.
q_cost_of_living.3: Cut the gas tax by 10 cents a litre, cap store markups on milk, eggs and poultry, and freeze car insurance rates.
q_cost_of_living.4: Suspend 10 cents a litre of fuel tax and cap gas station margins, cap margins on dairy, eggs and poultry, and freeze ICBC rates.
q_cost_of_living.5: Suspend 10 cents a litre of fuel tax with a BC Utilities Commission cap on gas margins, cap dairy, egg and poultry margins, and freeze ICBC rates until 2030.

q_cost_of_living.1: Give more help to people with the lowest incomes, paid for by the richest.
q_cost_of_living.2: Raise government support for the poorest people to the poverty line, paid for by a tax on the very rich.
q_cost_of_living.3: Raise income assistance to the poverty line and make transit free for young people and seniors, paid for by a tax on large fortunes.
q_cost_of_living.4: Raise income assistance to the poverty line, move toward a living wage, and make transit free for people under 25 and over 65, paid for by a wealth tax.
q_cost_of_living.5: Index income assistance to the Market Basket Measure poverty line, move the minimum wage toward a living wage, make transit free under 25 and over 65, and tax net worth over $50 million.

q_cost_of_living.1: Undo this year's tax rise and give renters a bigger tax break.
q_cost_of_living.2: Undo this year's rise in the lowest tax rate, raise the renter's credit, and cap Hydro and car insurance increases.
q_cost_of_living.3: Reverse the 2026 rise in the lowest tax rate, raise the renter's credit, add a transit-pass credit, cap Hydro and car insurance increases.
q_cost_of_living.4: Return the lowest tax rate to 5.06%, raise the renter's credit to $600, add a 15% transit and ferry pass credit, cap Hydro and ICBC increases at inflation, and widen PST relief on machinery.
q_cost_of_living.5: Cut the first tax bracket from 5.60% to 5.06% in January 2027, raise the renter's credit to $600 (indexed, full up to $80,000 income), add a 15% refundable commuter credit, and hold Hydro and ICBC increases at or below inflation.

q_taxes_deficit.1: Cut taxes a lot and spend much less, to stop borrowing within four years.
q_taxes_deficit.2: Cut everyone's taxes deeply and cut spending, so the budget balances within four years.
q_taxes_deficit.3: Cut every income tax rate by 25% and cut spending enough to balance the budget within four years.
q_taxes_deficit.4: Cut every income tax bracket by 25% and the PST by two points, with a firm target to balance the budget within four years.
q_taxes_deficit.5: Cut every personal and corporate bracket by 25% and the PST by two points, balance the budget within four years, and put part of any surplus toward debt.

q_taxes_deficit.1: Cut taxes a little and let a growing economy close the gap over time.
q_taxes_deficit.2: Cut taxes by about $1,000 per worker, add no new taxes, and let job growth close the gap over time.
q_taxes_deficit.3: Give a $1,000 income tax cut, add no new taxes, protect health funding, and rely on growth instead of a date to balance.
q_taxes_deficit.4: A $1,000-per-taxpayer income tax cut, a no-new-taxes pledge and a promise to protect current health funding, with resource growth to close the gap and no deficit target.
q_taxes_deficit.5: Raise the basic personal amount to $32,000 (not costed; estimates run from about $2 billion to $2.5 billion a year), add no new or higher taxes, protect current health funding, and rely on resource-led growth, with no balance date.

q_taxes_deficit.1: By law, stop borrowing in about eight years. Undo this year's tax rise.
q_taxes_deficit.2: Balance the budget by law in about eight years, undo this year's tax rise, and cut government jobs without layoffs.
q_taxes_deficit.3: Write a 2034-35 balanced budget into law, undo the 2026 rise in the lowest tax rate, and shrink the public service as people leave.
q_taxes_deficit.4: Legislate a balanced budget by 2034-35, checked by an Independent Budget Officer, return the lowest tax rate to 5.06%, cut 10,000 public positions through attrition, and review all spending.
q_taxes_deficit.5: A Balanced Budget and Spending Control Act (balance in 2034-35, an Independent Budget Officer, ministers' pay at risk), the first bracket back to 5.06%, 10,000 positions cut by attrition, and zero-based spending reviews.

q_taxes_deficit.1: Keep borrowing so schools and hospitals are not cut. Top earners pay more tax.
q_taxes_deficit.2: Keep borrowing to protect services, keep this year's tax changes, and raise taxes on top earners.
q_taxes_deficit.3: Keep borrowing to protect services, keep the 2026 rise in the lowest tax rate, and tax top earners more.
q_taxes_deficit.4: Run deficits above $11 billion a year instead of cutting services, shrink the public service through attrition, keep the Budget 2026 tax measures, and raise rates on income above $190,405.
q_taxes_deficit.5: Run deficits of $13.3 billion, $12.2 billion and $11.4 billion (Budget 2026 figures; the first is now forecast at $13.8 billion), cut 15,000 full-time-equivalent positions, keep the Budget 2026 tax measures, and raise the top two brackets by two points, with 24.5% above $1 million.

q_taxes_deficit.1: A new tax on the richest pays for child care, transit, housing and debt.
q_taxes_deficit.2: Tax people worth over $50 million and spend the money on child care, transit, housing and paying down debt.
q_taxes_deficit.3: Tax fortunes over $50 million and use the money for child care, transit, housing and debt.
q_taxes_deficit.4: A one-time, then yearly, wealth tax above $50 million, plus a windfall tax and higher resource royalties, with revenue split between programs and debt.
q_taxes_deficit.5: Tax net worth above $50 million (one-time 5%, 10% or 20% by tier, then 2%, 3% or 5% a year), add a windfall tax and 50% net-profit royalties, and fund programs and debt.

q_housing.1: Cut fees, taxes and rules on building, and add no new housing taxes.
q_housing.2: Cut taxes, fees and rules on building so builders build more, and add no new housing taxes.
q_housing.3: Cut taxes, fees and red tape on building, and add no new housing taxes.
q_housing.4: Cut fees and approval delays, drop new housing taxes, and return Metro Vancouver's housing role to the province and cities.
q_housing.5: Reject the Unsold Condo Tax and a higher speculation tax, cut permit times and development charges, and remove Metro Vancouver's housing role.

q_housing.1: Tax empty homes more, and make cities allow more homes on each lot.
q_housing.2: Raise taxes on empty and unsold homes, and make cities allow more homes on each lot.
q_housing.3: Raise taxes on empty homes and unsold condos, keep the tax on quick resales, and keep rules that make cities allow more homes.
q_housing.4: Raise the speculation tax, add a tax on unsold condos, and keep the flipping tax and provincial rules for four homes per lot and density near transit.
q_housing.5: Raise the speculation and vacancy tax to 2% (5% for foreign owners), add an Unsold Condo Tax from 2%, keep the flipping tax, Bills 44 and 47 and municipal targets, and continue BC Builds.

q_housing.1: Build many more non-profit homes. Limit rent increases when a new renter moves in.
q_housing.2: Build thousands of non-profit homes a year, and keep rent limits when a new renter moves in.
q_housing.3: Build or protect about 26,000 non-profit and public homes a year, and keep rent limits when a new renter moves in.
q_housing.4: Public and non-profit building and protection of about 26,000 affordable homes a year, a restarted Community Housing Fund, and vacancy control so rent limits stay between tenants.
q_housing.5: Set a goal of building and protecting 26,000 non-market homes a year, restart the Community and Indigenous Housing Funds, bring in vacancy control, and pay for it with a wealth levy and land tax.

q_housing.1: Give cities deadlines to approve homes, cut fees on rentals, build homes in factories.
q_housing.2: Set deadlines for city permits, halve fees on new rentals, build factory-made homes, and build more below-market homes.
q_housing.3: Set provincial deadlines for city approvals, halve development fees on rentals, build factory-made homes, and double below-market building.
q_housing.4: Set six-month rezoning and eight-week permit deadlines, halve development charges on rentals, build 5,000 factory-built homes a year, double the below-market program, and add no new housing taxes.
q_housing.5: Set a 2028 standard of six-month rezonings and eight-week permits with fee refunds if missed, halve development charges on rental and below-market homes, build 5,000 prefab homes a year, and grow BC Builds to 20,000 by 2031.

q_housing.1: Drop energy-saving building rules that add cost, and stop cities from limiting rent.
q_housing.2: Remove energy-efficiency rules for new buildings that raise costs, and stop cities from limiting rent.
q_housing.3: Scrap the Step Code, BC's energy rules for new buildings, and block cities from bringing in rent control.
q_housing.4: Eliminate the BC Energy Step Code, pass a law against municipal rent control, and rely on the market to add supply.
q_housing.5: Eliminate the BC Energy Step Code, prohibit municipal rent control, and rely on market supply with no demand-side taxes or zoning mandates.

q_health.1: Open more public clinics and train more doctors, paid for by top earners.
q_health.2: Open more public clinics, train more doctors, buy more scanners, and raise taxes on top earners.
q_health.3: Expand the public system with more clinics, training seats and scanners, paid for by higher taxes on top earners.
q_health.4: Scale up public care and testing with 20 clinics, 1,000 training seats and more MRI and CT scanners, paid for by a higher top tax rate.
q_health.5: Expand the public system with 20 clinics, a bridge for foreign-trained doctors, 1,000 training seats, 8 MRIs, 10 CT scanners and regional waitlists, keep the LFP pay model, and raise top tax brackets.

q_health.1: Care stays free. Families can pick approved care homes, run by government or not.
q_health.2: Care stays free, public money follows patients to approved providers, even company-run ones, and emergency rooms stay open.
q_health.3: Public funding follows patients to approved non-government providers, and an emergency fund keeps emergency rooms open.
q_health.4: Public funding with mixed delivery: protect current spending, a $50 million emergency fund, a 100-day wait-time commission, and long-term and home-care funding that follows the patient.
q_health.5: Universal public funding with mixed delivery: current funding protected, a $50 million health care emergency fund, a 100-day wait-time commission, and long-term and home-care funding patients can take to any qualified provider.

q_health.1: People can pay to get care faster. Free care stays for everyone else.
q_health.2: Let private clinics charge people who want to be seen sooner, alongside the free public system.
q_health.3: Allow private-pay care alongside the public system so people can pay for faster treatment.
q_health.4: Add a private-pay option for services the public plan covers, alongside the public system, and loosen rules on health professions to add capacity.
q_health.5: Allow a parallel private tier for services the Medical Services Plan insures and repeal the Health Professions and Occupations Act, which needs the Medicare Protection Act amended or left unenforced.

q_health.1: A public health centre in every community, and no private nursing companies.
q_health.2: A public health centre in every area, and no more hiring nurses through private agencies.
q_health.3: Public care only: a community health centre in every riding, no private agency nurses, and public mental health care.
q_health.4: Public delivery only: a community health centre in every riding, full nurse-to-patient ratios, no agency nurses, and public coverage for counselling.
q_health.5: A community health centre in every riding, nurse-to-patient ratios completed, agency nursing phased out, mental health care in the public plan, and single-entry surgical referral.

q_health.1: Give everyone a regular doctor or nurse, paid for by cutting health office costs.
q_health.2: A doctor or nurse practitioner for everyone, more surgeries and care homes, paid for by cutting health office costs.
q_health.3: A doctor or nurse practitioner for everyone by 2031, a law on emergency room closures, more surgeries and care beds, and fewer health executives.
q_health.4: A primary-care team for everyone by 2031, an ER Accountability Act, 15,000 more surgeries a year and 2,500 care beds started, paid for by merging health-authority back offices, with no private pay.
q_health.5: Team-based care for everyone by 2031 with automatic registration, 600 nurse practitioners, an ER Accountability Act, 15,000 more surgeries, 2,500 long-term care beds under construction and one health-authority back office, with no private pay.

q_dripa.1: End the law, and stop new deals that give First Nations land or money.
q_dripa.2: Cancel the law, declare that the United Nations declaration does not apply in BC, and stop land and money transfers.
q_dripa.3: Repeal the law, declare the United Nations Declaration of no effect in BC, and stop voluntary land and money transfers.
q_dripa.4: Repeal DRIPA, declare the UN Declaration (UNDRIP) of no force in BC, end voluntary cash, land and resource transfers, and seek repeal of the Indian Act.
q_dripa.5: Repeal DRIPA and section 8.1 of the Interpretation Act, declare UNDRIP of no force in BC, freeze voluntary transfers, and repeal the Indian Act.

q_dripa.1: End the law, but keep partnering with First Nations on projects and jobs.
q_dripa.2: Cancel the law, but keep making project deals with First Nations that create jobs.
q_dripa.3: Repeal the law and rely instead on project partnerships with First Nations, with no new law to replace it.
q_dripa.4: Repeal DRIPA, pursue economic reconciliation through project partnerships with First Nations, and pass no replacement law.
q_dripa.5: Repeal DRIPA and pursue economic reconciliation by building projects with First Nations, with no replacement law, while section 35 duties continue.

q_dripa.1: Keep the law, but stop judges from using it to strike down other laws.
q_dripa.2: Keep the law, but change it, working with First Nations, so courts cannot strike down other laws.
q_dripa.3: Amend the law, in talks with First Nations, so courts cannot use it to strike down other laws.
q_dripa.4: Amend DRIPA so courts cannot enforce the duty to align laws, keep consent agreements, and negotiate the change with First Nations leaders.
q_dripa.5: Amend the DRIPA alignment duty and the Interpretation Act provision so courts cannot enforce them, keep section 7 agreements, and negotiate with the First Nations Leadership Council.

q_dripa.1: Replace the law with a new one based on treaties, and protect people's homes.
q_dripa.2: Replace the law with one focused on reaching treaties, and promise no family loses their home over a land ruling.
q_dripa.3: Repeal the law and replace it with a treaty-based law, protect private land and homeowners, and let the legislature, not courts, decide.
q_dripa.4: Repeal DRIPA and replace it with a treaty-based law: $30 million a year for treaty talks, homeowner compensation after title rulings, no private land transferred without a willing owner, and deals published before signing.
q_dripa.5: Repeal DRIPA and section 8.1 of the Interpretation Act, pass a treaty-based law funded at $30 million a year, treat UNDRIP 'as a guide', compensate homeowners up to assessed value, and publish agreements 60 days before signing.

q_dripa.1: Make the law stronger, with a clear plan and public education about it.
q_dripa.2: Make the law stronger, with a clear plan to carry it out, public education and expert advisers.
q_dripa.3: Strengthen the law with a new law setting out how to carry it out, public education, and an expert advisory committee.
q_dripa.4: Pass a law to carry out DRIPA, fund public education, create an expert advisory committee, and oppose any suspension or weakening.
q_dripa.5: Pass a DRIPA Implementation Act that sets out alignment and reporting, fund public education, create an expert advisory committee, oppose suspension, and follow the First Nations Leadership Council proposal.

q_sogi.1: Remove all lessons on gender identity from schools, and pass a parents' rights law.
q_sogi.2: Remove SOGI 123 and all lessons on gender identity, and pass a law on parents' rights.
q_sogi.3: Repeal SOGI 123, remove all gender-identity content from schools, and pass a parental rights law.
q_sogi.4: Repeal SOGI 123, remove all gender-identity content from curriculum and resources, and pass a Parental Bill of Rights.
q_sogi.5: Repeal SOGI 123, remove all gender-identity content from kindergarten to Grade 12, and pass a Parental Bill of Rights.

q_sogi.1: End these lessons, focus on reading and math, and keep every student safe.
q_sogi.2: End SOGI 123, focus on reading, writing and math, and keep every student safe from bullying.
q_sogi.3: Repeal SOGI 123, refocus schools on reading, writing and math, and keep schools safe for all students.
q_sogi.4: Repeal SOGI 123, replace it with general anti-bullying rules, and refocus on reading, writing and math.
q_sogi.5: Repeal SOGI 123, remove derived lesson plans and policy guides, adopt zero-tolerance anti-bullying rules, and refocus on reading, writing and arithmetic.
